title: bug: grantNextLeases passes over a worktree completion's queued git-land lease, because complete_task already cleared the task's assignee
description:
Filed by the governor on 2026-11-03 from a live stall of WT-19 (task-b1ca54f2), the worktree epic's final task.

PROBLEM. A worktree completion takes the git-land-<target> lease at L3, after moe.complete_task has moved the row to REVIEW and cleared assignedWorkerId. If another landing holds the lease, the wrapper queues (acquire_resource, then wait_for_resource). On release, grantNextLeases (packages/moe-daemon/src/state/resourceStore.ts, the pass-over at ~line 449) skips every entry whose task fails heldByLiveSeat (~line 83). heldByLiveSeat returns false for any unassigned task. So the queued completion is never granted:
- it waits out its own wait_for_resource (up to 10 min per wait);
- later landings acquire directly past it;
- under steady traffic it can exhaust MOE_LAND_LEASE_WAIT_SEC (default 1800) and fail as MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_LAND_LEASE, the unlanded route back to a worker.

EVIDENCE. From .moe/activity.log, 2026-11-03, git-land-moe-work-2026-10-24:
- 13:54:56Z RESOURCE_ACQUIRED task-1765335a (worker-ed0f6a9e).
- 13:55:17Z RESOURCE_QUEUED task-b1ca54f2 (worker-8cf0816c). WT-19 is REVIEW with no assignee: complete_task ran at 13:54:54Z.
- 13:55:24Z RESOURCE_RELEASED task-1765335a. No grant follows.
- 13:57:37Z RESOURCE_ACQUIRED task-13ff6bb4 (direct, past the queued WT-19).
- 13:58:01Z RESOURCE_RELEASED task-13ff6bb4. Still no grant.
- At 14:04Z, list_resources showed holders [] and queue [task-b1ca54f2, position 1]. The wrapper was still parked in wait_for_resource.

FIX DIRECTION (verify against the code first).
- A queue entry is held for grant purposes when either:
  - the task's assignee is a live seat bound to it (as today); or
  - the entry's own workerId is a registered, non-DEAD seat that owns the task's open execution attempt in `finalizing`. That is the post-complete_task landing window, the one moe.finalize_attempt closes.
- Keep the pass-over for rows nobody can use, so resourceStore.unheld.test.ts stays meaningful.
- Assumption to check: which attempt-store accessor exposes an attempt's status and its owning worker.

Files expected: packages/moe-daemon/src/state/resourceStore.ts plus a test (a resourceStore*.test.ts file or a new one). Not held by any open row at filing time.
definitionOfDone: When a task in REVIEW has an open finalizing attempt owned by a live seat, and that seat's git-land queue entry comes up, grantNextLeases grants it as capacity frees and logs RESOURCE_GRANTED. A regression test replays the 13:55Z sequence: A holds the lease; B completes, so it is unassigned with a finalizing attempt, and queues; A releases; B is granted.

Rows no live seat can use are still passed over: unassigned with no finalizing attempt, a DEAD or deregistered requester, or an attempt owned by another seat. The existing resourceStore tests (unheld, lifecycle, deregister, durability) stay green.

The daemon's resourceStore test files and its full npm test pass in a git archive or clone snapshot outside the shared checkout (global rail), with error handling for a missing or unreadable attempt record that falls back to today's pass-over.

implementationPlan.description: Fix with error handling in packages/moe-daemon/src/state/resourceStore.ts. (1) import { currentAttempt } from './attemptStore.js' (state to state; attemptStore imports nothing from resourceStore, so no cycle). (2) heldByLiveSeat(state, task, requesterId: string): keep the assignee branch exactly as today (assignee set and its worker record missing, or not DEAD with currentTaskId === task.id, returns true); in every other case return landingSeatHoldsTask(state, task, requesterId). It is an OR, so a DEAD or elsewhere-bound assignee also falls through. (3) New private landingSeatHoldsTask(state, task, requesterId), the post-complete_task landing window: const seat = state.getWorker(requesterId); return false when the record is missing (a deregistered requester: unlike the assignee branch, no record is NOT granted) or DEAD. This seat lookup runs BEFORE the attempt comparison, so an entry with a blank workerId can never match a malformed attempt's missing workerId. Then try { const attempt = currentAttempt(state, task.id); return attempt?.phase === 'finalizing' && attempt.workerId === requesterId; } catch (error) { logger.warn({ taskId: task.id, workerId: requesterId, error }, 'grantNextLeases: attempt record unreadable; passing the queue entry over'); return false; }. A missing attempt is null, so false: today's pass-over. Do NOT require seat.currentTaskId === task.id (complete_task leaves the seat IDLE with currentTaskId null, completeTask.ts touchWorker) and do NOT filter on task status (isResourceTaskEligible already does). (4) grantNextLeases call site (~line 449): heldByLiveSeat(state, task, next.workerId). (5) Update the three comments that describe the pass-over (file header ~18-24, heldByLiveSeat's JSDoc, the block above passedOver ~435-439): a row also counts as held while the entry's own registered, non-DEAD seat owns the task's finalizing attempt (complete_task cleared the assignee; the worktree wrapper takes git-land at L3 inside that window, which moe.finalize_attempt closes). Leave acquireResource, releaseResource, releaseDeregisteredClaims, reapResources, restoreUnheldTask and resumeResourceHolder unchanged: a granted REVIEW row is not BLOCKED, so resumeResourceHolder only posts the green grant line and repairs no seat. Re-run step 1's test in the snapshot: it must pass now.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Chosen: OR a landing rule into heldByLiveSeat, keyed on the queue entry's own workerId owning the task's finalizing attempt (the governor's fix direction). (2) util/claimEligibility.ts finalizingAttemptsByTask (a validated index): rejected. It is util-layer, and it copies and indexes every attempt of every task per call. currentAttempt from the same state layer reads one task, and the registered-seat check plus exact workerId equality already reject malformed records. (3) Grant any unassigned row whose requester is a live seat, with no attempt check: rejected, because it reintroduces idle leases for released rows and undoes 9ca72836. (4) Require an active wait_for_resource waiter: rejected. It is a state-to-tools layer violation, and it races across the wrapper's acquire/wait round trips. (5) Make acquireResource's direct grant respect older passed-over entries: out of scope. With this fix the landing is granted at release, so the jump-past window (13:57:37Z) closes for this case.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: complete_task (completeTask.ts:271-301) sets the open attempt to finalizing BEFORE the WORKING-to-REVIEW updateTask that clears assignedWorkerId, then touchWorker(..., { status: 'IDLE', currentTaskId: null }). While the attempt is finalizing, every other seat's claim is refused or skips the row (claimEligibility.ts foreignFinalizingAttempt), and the worker's own next claim is refused, so the requester cannot be bound to another task. The worktree wrapper's L3 lease calls (moe-agent.sh land_lease_rpc ~7621) send workerId=$WORKER_ID and taskId=$LAND_TASK_ID, so the queue entry's workerId equals the attempt's workerId. wait_for_resource resolves on a RESOURCE_UPDATED whose holders include its taskId (waitForResource.ts:144-151), so the grant alone un-parks the wrapper. assertWorkerOwns is a no-op on unassigned rows, which is why acquire and wait still work after complete_task.
